citations.narrative:
The facility exhibits animals in a manner that does not pose minimal risk of harm to the animals and members of the
public. The inspector witnessed a boy and teenaged girl each participate in separate full-contact sessions inside an
enclosure with one approximately 5-month-old male ring-tailed lemur and one approximately 4-month-old female ring-
tailed lemur. The only employee of the store remained outside the enclosure, unable to reach the animal without opening
the door. The animals freely jumped onto the arms, shoulders and heads of the children, at times pressing their faces very
close and even touching the heads and faces of the children. The girl jerked her head back a few times in response to a
lemur touching her face-to-face and the boy was seen turning his face away as a lemur touched the boy’s head and face
while it sat on his shoulder. The inspector spoke to the licensee by phone directly after the encounters, and the licensee
told the inspector that the store would no longer offer these contact encounters.
Allowing animals to climb on the heads, necks, and shoulders of the public and make facial contact is not a method of
handling that promotes minimal risk to the public and to the animal. Such interactions pose a threat of zoonotic disease
transmission and can lead to injury of the animals and/or the public if the animal becomes afraid or surprised. The
licensee must ensure that during public exhibition, any animal must be handled so there is minimal risk of harm to the
animal and to the public, with sufficient distance and/or barriers between the animal and the general viewing public to
assure the safety of animals and the public.
CORRECTED AT THE TIME OF THIS INSPECTION ON 09/02/2026

During a paid, full-contact animal encounter between the public and two, young ring-tailed lemurs, the only store
employee present asked the inspector if she (the store employee) could leave to give fresh water to other animals in the
store. In response, the inspector said that the employee should not leave during the encounters and asked if direct public
contact is allowed without supervision of a store employee. The store employee replied that she sometimes has to step
away to help other customers for no more than two minutes when she is the only one working, and that she asks the
encounter participants to call out for her if anything seems to be going wrong. The inspector spoke to the licensee by
phone directly after the encounters, and the licensee told the inspector that the store would no longer offer these contact
encounters.
Lack of employee oversight during direct interactions between the animals and the public may lead to injury to people
and/or injury or distress to the animals. A responsible, knowledgeable, and readily identifiable employee or attendant must
be present at all times during periods of public contact.
CORRECTED AT THE TIME OF THIS INSPECTION ON 09/02/2026
This inspection and exit interview were conducted with a facility representative and the licensee.
